question: How do CUDA streams, events, the stream-ordered allocator, CUDA Graph capture and programmatic dependent launch hide latency between kernels, between host and GPU, and across GPUs?
contributions: Explains overlap of H2D copy, compute and D2H copy with streams, pinned memory and cudaMallocAsync
Compares legacy default, per-thread default and explicit streams, with best practices
Shows event-based cross-stream and cross-GPU synchronisation, NCCL/NIXL stream use and CUDA Graph capture of a multi-stream iteration
Layers inter-kernel streams on the Chapter 10 warp-specialised and thread-block-cluster kernels

practices: Create explicit nondefault streams with cudaStreamNonBlocking and never put performance-critical work in legacy stream 0 (Best Practices for Default Stream Usage).
Enable per-thread default streams (nvcc --default-stream per-thread) when multiple host threads enqueue GPU work (Modern Per-Thread Default Stream).
Use pinned host memory for cudaMemcpyAsync so copies overlap compute (Using Streams to Overlap Compute with Data Transfers).
Use cudaMallocAsync/cudaFreeAsync in the stream that uses the buffer, and tune cudaMemPoolAttrReleaseThreshold (Stream-Ordered Memory Allocator).
Coordinate streams with cudaEventRecord and cudaStreamWaitEvent, not cudaDeviceSynchronize or default-stream sync (Fine-Grained Synchronization with Events and Callbacks).
Do not call CUDA APIs inside a cudaLaunchHostFunc callback; limit it to CPU-side work (same section).
Give NCCL/NIXL communication streams higher priority so they are not queued behind big compute kernels (Multi-GPU Compute and Data Transfer Overlap).
Capture a whole iteration into a CUDA Graph to remove per-launch overhead (Multi-GPU section; detailed in Chapter 12).
Use two or three streams cycled round-robin; query asyncEngineCount; keep chunks neither too small nor too large (Stream-Ordered Memory Allocator).
Prefer double-buffered kernels or two-stage pipelines with streams over warp specialization plus clusters for most LLM workloads (Warp Specialization with Thread Block Clusters and CUDA Streams).
For PDL, trigger Kernel B only after Kernel A has produced and synchronised all data B needs (Programmatic Dependent Launch).

terms.definition: A sequence of operations—kernel launches, memory copies, and memory allocations—that execute in the order they are issued.

terms.definition: Stream 0; any operation launched into it waits for all previously enqueued work in every other stream, and vice versa, acting as a global barrier.
Each host thread has its own implicit stream 0 that does not wait on other threads' default streams.
